Class RmiVirtualServer

java.lang.Object
network.client.rmi.RmiVirtualServer
All Implemented Interfaces:
VirtualServer
public class RmiVirtualServer extends Object implements VirtualServer
RMI implementation of the client-side VirtualServer proxy.

Lifecycle:

  1. RmiVirtualServer(String, int) looks up the server stub in the RMI registry. No callback is exported and no join call is made at this stage.
  2. tryRegisterName(String, LocalGameState, ClientStateListener) exports a fresh ClientCallbackImpl bound to the given local-state/listener pair and calls serverStub.join(...). If the server rejects the name (already taken), the callback is unexported and the method returns false so the caller can retry with a different name.
  3. start() starts the bidirectional liveness sentinel.

The exported callback object owns an RMI listener thread that keeps the JVM alive. close() explicitly unexports it to allow clean process termination.

    • SEND_INTERVAL_MS

      private static final long SEND_INTERVAL_MS
      Client-side RMI liveness intervals (milliseconds). Invariant: TIMEOUT_MS > 2 * SEND_INTERVAL_MS, to tolerate scheduling jitter and brief delays from large application messages occupying the sender. Worst-case detection time is TIMEOUT_MS + CHECK_INTERVAL_MS = 20 s.

  • Method Details

    • tryRegisterName

      public boolean tryRegisterName(String name, LocalGameState localState, ClientStateListener listener)
      RMI name handshake: exports a fresh ClientCallbackImpl and calls serverStub.join(...). On rejection the callback is unexported at once, so a retry exports a clean one. No reader thread is involved — the RMI runtime drives inbound callbacks.
      Specified by:
      tryRegisterName in interface VirtualServer
      Parameters:
      name - the requested player name
      localState - the local state to be updated from server snapshots
      listener - the listener notified of inbound server events
      Returns:
      true if the server accepted the name and registered the player; false if the name was already taken (caller may retry with a different name).

    • start

      public void start()
      Creates the single-thread command executor, starts the liveness sentinel and routes inbound notifications to it. No reader thread is spawned (the RMI runtime delivers callbacks). Call once, after a successful tryRegisterName(String, LocalGameState, ClientStateListener).
      Specified by:
      start in interface VirtualServer

    • onConnectionLost

      private void onConnectionLost()
      Invoked by the watchdog when the server sends no message within TIMEOUT_MS. Stops the sentinel, releases local resources and notifies the UI. Runs at most once (guarded by disconnected).

    • cleanupLocalResources

      private void cleanupLocalResources()
      Tears down the local resources (executor + exported callback) without notifying the server. Used both by close() after a successful session and by the constructor's failure path, where the server has no record of this client and a disconnect call would be incorrect.

    • submitAsync

      private void submitAsync(ClientCommand command)
      Serialises the given command onto the command executor. If the executor has already been shut down (because close() was called), the command is silently dropped.
